title: Geometry - Lesson 10 Practice: Two-Column Congruence Proofs
description: Practice choosing valid proof reasons, triangle congruence shortcuts, and CPCTC steps for two-column congruence proofs.

questions.question: Which reason justifies the statement $\overline{BC} \cong \overline{BC}$ in a triangle proof?
questions.explanation: A segment is congruent to itself by the Reflexive Property.

questions.question: You know two side pairs are congruent and the included angle pair is congruent. Which shortcut proves the triangles congruent?
questions.explanation: Two sides and the included angle prove triangle congruence by SAS.

questions.question: CPCTC can be used only after two triangles have already been proven congruent.
questions.explanation: CPCTC depends on a proven triangle congruence statement.

questions.question: SSA is always a valid triangle congruence shortcut.
questions.explanation: SSA is not a valid triangle congruence shortcut in general.

questions.question: The theorem that says vertical angles are congruent is the ______ Angles Theorem.
questions.explanation: The Vertical Angles Theorem states that vertical angles are congruent.

questions.question: In a two-column proof, the left column usually contains statements and the right column contains ______.
questions.explanation: Every proof statement needs a supporting reason.

questions.question: After proving $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$, what reason justifies $\overline{AC} \cong \overline{DF}$?
questions.correctAnswer: CPCTC, because corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent.
questions.explanation: Once triangle congruence is proven, matching sides and angles can be proven with CPCTC.

questions.question: Explain why 'the triangles look congruent' is not a valid proof reason.
questions.correctAnswer: A diagram may not be drawn accurately, so proof must use givens, markings, definitions, postulates, theorems, or properties rather than appearance.
questions.explanation: Geometry proofs require justified facts, not visual guesses from a sketch.
